correctness.rationale: The four gcd classes have the claimed totient sizes, and direct p- and q-adic valuation arithmetic shows that the only joins are A-B, B-C, and C-D, with B a clique. Each class is a twin class, so a forcing set can omit at most one vertex per class. Because A and D always have size at least two, blue endpoint representatives force possible whites in B and C first; then the now-blue middle classes force possible whites in A and D. This proves the factorized polynomial and minimum-set count. A nonsingular four-by-four symmetric class matrix gives a rank-four graph-pattern witness, while M<=Z supplies the reverse inequality.

value.rationale: Gamma(Z/(p^2 q)) is a standard arithmetic graph family with current homological literature. The result determines its entire zero forcing polynomial, every minimum forcing set, maximum nullity, and exact real minimum rank for all distinct primes. The closed factorization and rank witness constitute a natural complete classification at the first nonsquarefree two-prime exponent level.
